answer: The core defense is an identity cost that grows with repetition: each new agent must solve a unique, epoch-bound puzzle whose difficulty scales with how many keys were minted from the same operator cluster recently, so a sybil vine cannot branch cheaply. To reach the terrace of full voting rights, a key also needs a sustained streak of attestations from peers outside its cluster across several epochs. A single newcomer pays almost nothing; a farm pays at dawn on every branch, repeatedly.
